articles.title: Karnataka government serves show-cause notice to IOCL terminal in Bengaluru over ethanol measurement discrepancies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The action follows inspections initiated by the Department of Legal Metrology, Karnataka, at the terminals of oil marketing companies, taking the checks of fuel samples for ethanol blend one step further

The Karnataka government on Friday served a show-cause notice on Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) over discrepancies in the measurement of ethanol and motor gasoline at its terminal in Devanagonthi, Bengaluru, and directed the oil marketing company (OMC) to submit an explanation within seven days.
The action follows inspections initiated by the Department of Legal Metrology, Karnataka, at the terminals of oil marketing companies.

Tests of samples from petrol stations in Karnataka by the State government had revealed ethanol blending to be as high as 32% in some cases, Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology Minister Rizwan Arshad claimed earlier this month. This was denied by OMCs and Union Ministers.
Mr. Arshad had also written to the Union government seeking display of accurate ethanol blending in petrol at every station.

According to the show-cause notice, officials detected discrepancies in the quantities of ethanol and motor gasoline dispensed through mass flow meters during an inspection at the IOCL terminal on Wednesday (November 25).

According to the Minister, the inspection was conducted using the “master proving” test method. At Bay No. 9, officials found that the meter was dispensing 14 litres of ethanol in excess for every 3,000 litres. At the same bay, the quantity of motor gasoline supplied was found to be 4 to 6 litres short for every 3,000 litres. Another mass flow meter at Bay No. 4 was also found to be dispensing an additional three litres of ethanol for every 3,000 litres, the notice stated.

Mr. Arshad said that the discrepancies exceeded the permissible limits prescribed under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009, and the rules framed under it. “The inaccuracies in measurement could adversely affect the interests of consumers, distributors and other stakeholders dealing with petroleum products,” he said.

The show-cause notice, issued to the Deputy General Manager in charge of the Devanagonthi terminal, has sought a written explanation within seven days of its receipt, warning that failure to submit a satisfactory explanation within the stipulated period could lead to further legal and departmental action against the terminal and the officials responsible.

The department has asked IOCL to explain the reasons behind the discrepancies and provide details of the measures taken to ensure the accuracy of the mass flow meters and associated batch control units. It has also sought records of their latest calibration and maintenance, along with details of corrective measures proposed to address the discrepancies.
Further, the department has directed IOCL not to use the affected measurement systems for commercial transactions until their accuracy and compliance with prescribed legal standards are verified.

articles.title: Nagenthran, Annamalai welcome SC order on Thirupparankundram issue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran on Friday said Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should resign, in the light of the observations made by the Supreme Court in the Thirupparankundram issue.

In a social media post, Mr. Nagenthran said the apex court suspending the temple’s Board of Trustees and issuing show-cause notices on contempt against the Chief Secretary, DGP, authorities of the HR&CE Department, among others, was proof of the administrative failure of the government headed by Mr. Vijay.
The Supreme Court appointing High Court former judges as receivers to administer the temple, was a “befitting reply to the anti-Hindu attitude of the TVK government,” Mr. Nagenthran said.

He welcomed the apex court directing the deployment of the CRPF personnel in this issue. “After the strong observations of the Supreme Court, Mr. Joseph Vijay is not fit to continue as the Chief Minister,” he said.

We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai said he sincerely hoped the TVK government would desist from any further attempts to defy the court’s orders and stopped “playing with the faith and devotion of countless devotees of Lord Muruga across Tamil Nadu.”

In a social media post, Mr. Annamalai said: “We reiterate that the rule of law cannot be subject to the whims of those in power, whether you like it or not. At this juncture, I appeal to all political parties and religious organisations to step back and allow devotees of Lord Muruga, without any political or organisational affiliations, to light the lamp at the deepathoon .”

📰 Nagenthran, Annamalai welcome SC order on Thirupparankundram issue

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran on Friday said Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should resign, in the light of the observations made by the Supreme Court in the Thirupparankundram issue.

In a social media post, Mr. Nagenthran said the apex court suspending the temple’s Board of Trustees and issuing show-cause notices on contempt against the Chief Secretary, DGP, authorities of the HR&CE Department, among others, was proof of the administrative failure of the government headed by Mr. Vijay.

The Supreme Court appointing High Court former judges as receivers to administer the temple, was a “befitting reply to the anti-Hindu attitude of the TVK government,” Mr. Nagenthran said.

He welcomed the apex court directing the deployment of the CRPF personnel in this issue. “After the strong observations of the Supreme Court, Mr. Joseph Vijay is not fit to continue as the Chief Minister,” he said.

We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai said he sincerely hoped the TVK government would desist from any further attempts to defy the court’s orders and stopped “playing with the faith and devotion of countless devotees of Lord Muruga across Tamil Nadu.”

In a social media post, Mr. Annamalai said: “We reiterate that the rule of law cannot be subject to the whims of those in power, whether you like it or not. At this juncture, I appeal to all political parties and religious organisations to step back and allow devotees of Lord Muruga, without any political or organisational affiliations, to light the lamp at the deepathoon .”

articles.title: Civil society groups urge Karnataka Chief Minister to scrutinise SIR deletions ahead of local polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Members of various civil society groups under the banner of the “Anti-SIR alliance” on Friday submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, demanding that the State government reject the final electoral roll published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and take a clear stand against the exercise, with local body elections approaching.

The alliance said the final electoral roll was riddled with errors and demanded that the 2025 electoral roll be restored, subjected to public scrutiny and revised in a voter-friendly manner before being used for local body elections.

The alliance also cited the Election Commission’s recent instructions to States conducting SIR to “revisit deleted and left-out voters”, publish booth-wise deletion lists and make efforts to restore those wrongly excluded. It said these directions pointed to serious shortcomings in the SIR.

The groups, in their letter, also criticised statements by some Congress Ministers that Karnataka had not lost anything through SIR and could use the revised rolls for local body elections. The alliance said the government should not assess the exercise through the narrow lens of electoral gains or losses. It also pressed for a social audit to establish the legitimacy of deletions made during SIR.

articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.
High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. .
Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up. Edible oil prices recorded a broad-based increase, led by mustard oil, the RBI officials said in the State of the Economy article.

Vegetable prices presented a mixed picture, with onion prices rising moderately, tomato prices correcting sharply and potato prices picking up. The Indian basket of crude oil declined to $95 per barrel during November 1-18.
“The pressure on prices was primarily driven by ‘food and beverages’,” the officials pointed out.
Inflationary pressures were, however, not confined to food. Fuel and core inflation also firmed up, with 11 of the 12 CPI divisions registering sequential increases in October.

Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick.

Geographically, inflation increased in both rural and urban areas in October, with food and beverages inflation remaining above 6% in both segments. While most States and Union Territories recorded inflation in the 4-6% range, the number reporting rates above 6% increased.

On the external front, geopolitical instability in West Asia continued to weigh on the global economic outlook. Although crude oil prices retreated from their October peaks, the absence of a durable peace kept markets volatile. “Apart from extant geopolitical risks, the recent pullback in AI stocks lends uncertainty to the global financial outlook,” the officials said.

Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.
“The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday.

A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market.

The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun.

The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.

articles.title: Pressure tactics: On the new U.S. tariffs on India
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014.

Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

📰 Pressure tactics: On the new U.S. tariffs on India

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014.

Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

articles.title: Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu should have followed Court order without backing Deepathoon claim

By defying the Supreme Court’s one-time direction to also light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar , claimed by Hindu groups to be a Deepathoon, atop the Thirupparankundram hills, the Tamil Nadu government has disregarded a constitutional body’s authority. Believed to be Lord Murugan’s first abode, the hills have, for centuries , witnessed an intersection of religious faiths, with occasional skirmishes leading to tense flare-ups and legal battles. They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights.

Against this backdrop, last year, the Madras High Cour t’s Madurai Bench, relying on the 1931 Privy Council ruling on ownership of the hills, held that “for the sake of protecting its property, the [Subramania Swamy] temple management is obliged to light the festival lamp at the Deepathoon” . The DMK government defied the order. Later, a Division Bench upheld the verdict. While staying this order recently, the Supreme Court cited the festival’s proximity to permit the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon this year alone , clarifying that this did not constitute “essential religious practice”. The State filed a review petition , arguing when no right is recognised prima facie, a direction altering the existing position lacks judicial foundation. On Karthigai Deepam day, November 24, with the review pending, the government walked a tightrope. The Collector assured the High Court of compliance. Yet, the lamp was lit only at the traditional spot . The Collector has now apologised to the Court, blaming the temple’s Board of Trustees for not authorising the proposed lighting team at the Deepathoon. The administration has thus attempted to distinguish its proclaimed intent to comply with judicial directions from customs governed by the trustees. But it remains exposed to the charge of colluding with the temple authorities to breach a judicial mandate. The Deepathoon may be a mischievous prop deployed by self-serving Hindu groups, but the pillar stands on temple property. The State could have permitted the limited lighting, leaving the onus on the Court, without endorsing the Deepathoon claim or compromising religious amity. A democracy can remain healthy only when its constitutional pillars do not collide with one another.

articles.title: Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday.

The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurating an international conference on Arabic at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN

Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke.
E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world.
Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

articles.title: BDO issues residence certificate to mother of child denied birth certificate due to SIR row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib were denied a residence proof necessary for birth certificate on grounds that Abdul Habib’s name was struck off electoral rolls during SIR.

The district administration of Coochbehar district in West Bengal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) issued a residence certificate to the mother of a two-month-old infant, after her parents faced challenges to get the certificate on the ground that the name of the father was deleted from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) held earlier this year.

The Hindu reported on November 25 that the birth certificate was denied to the infant because the father's name was deleted from the electoral roll during SIR. Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, gave birth to a girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital on September 9. Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib approached the hospital and the concerned panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. The couple was reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the local panchayat pradhan or MLA.

On the grounds that the name of Abdul Habib was deleted from the electoral roll in the SIR, the local BJP MLA office refused to give them residence proof. On Thursday (November 26), the BDO office issued a residence certificate to Amina Khatun.

“This is to certify that Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, is a permanent resident of village Khatamari P.O. Khatamari as per the enquiry report of Chowdhurihat Gram Panchayat -. Under Dinhata-II Development Block, P.S.: Sahebganj, Dist.: Cooch Behar. The name of the applicant has been enrolled in the Electoral Roll vide Part-191, Sl. No .848 of 7 Dinhata Assembly Constituency. I wish him/her all success in his/her life,” read the certificate issued by the BDO on Thursday.

Abdul Hamid told this correspondent that government officials came to his residence and took him to the BDO office where the residence proof was given to him. “I have received my residence verification certificate which I am going to submit at the hospital tomorrow. Hopefully, my daughter will now get the birth certificate soon,” the father said.

There have been allegations of denial of services by the West Bengal government to citizens whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls during SIR. The Supreme Court, which oversaw the SIR process in the State, had made it clear that removal of a name from the electoral roll cannot be grounds for denial of services. The names of about 36 lakh electors deleted during SIR are pending before SIR tribunals in the State.
Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India / government

articles.title: Karnataka Industries Minister holds talks with four Japanese companies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans

Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies on Thursday, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans.

According to a release, during a meeting with Seiren Co. Ltd., a manufacturer of automotive interior materials, discussions focused on its manufacturing operations at the Kadakola Industrial Area in Mysuru and its plans to expand its presence in line with Toyota’s growing capacity in the State.

At a meeting with the leadership of Enomoto Co. Ltd., a Japanese manufacturer of precision connector components and semiconductor lead frames, discussions centred on potential expansion locations, including the Tumakuru Machine Tool Park and the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

In a meeting with representatives of Secom and Toyota Tsusho Corporation, the Minister discussed the growth plans of Sakra World Hospital. Discussions were also held with Makino, a leading manufacturer of high-precision machine tools, the release said.

articles.title: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government trying to pass the Bill after ‘operation lotus’, says Congress
The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill.

The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13.

Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008 , when it went on for 87 days.

The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001.

Reacting to the announcement, Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Narendra Modi government announced the session “after 105 days of operation lotus” in the hope of getting a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to get the Bill passed. “Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution,” he asked in a post on X, noting that the announcement came on Constitution Day.
Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal took to X to describe the attempt to pass the Delimitation Bill as “ sansad chori” .
“To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass,” Mr. Venugopal said.

Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions.

Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill.
In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight.

articles.title: Sthaneeka Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: On November 24, the Executive Officer of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. But a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent, went viral on social media the next day

The Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram gave some tense moments to the Madurai district administration by making contradictory statements on their “consent” for lighting the ceremonial lamp at the traditional spot — Deepa Mandapam — on Karthigai Deepam day.
Editorial | Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order

The administration had submitted at the Supreme Court that despite its readiness to light the lamp at the deepathoon , it could not comply with the court directive as the temple’s Board of Trustees insisted on lighting the lamp only at the Deepa Mandapam, following age-old practices, customs and rituals, and agama rules.

A statement made on November 24 by the temple’s Executive Officer, G. Selvi, had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. However, the next day, a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent on lighting the lamp on November 24, went viral on social media. articles.title: Constitution is the guiding force for present, future, says Haryana CM Saini; Congress accuses BJP of undermining democracy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Respecting the Constitution is not the responsibility of any one political party or government, but the duty of every individual whom the people have entrusted with the opportunity to serve them, said Nayab Singh Saini

Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said that the Constitution is the guiding force for our present and future, which has shown the country the right path in overcoming every challenge, even as the Congress party accused the BJP of undermining democratic conventions, the independence of constitutional institutions and the voting rights of citizens.

“Over the past 77 years, the Constitution has shown the country the right path in overcoming every challenge. Respecting the Constitution is not the responsibility of any one political party or government, but the duty of every individual whom the people have entrusted with the opportunity to serve them,” said Mr. Saini, addressing the House during the special session of the Haryana State Assembly on the 77th anniversary of the adoption of the Constitution.

He said that the true tribute to the framers of the Constitution would be to uphold the democratic path shown by them, maintain its decorum and contribute to building an India where justice is accessible to all, opportunities are available to everyone and the dignity of every citizen is protected.

Meanwhile, as part of the party’s nationwide demonstration, Haryana Congress organised a ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’ in Panchkula. Led by AICC In-charge for Haryana Sanjay Dutt, Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee President Rao Narender Singh, and Congress Legislature Party Leader and former Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, the march drew senior party leaders.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Dutt said that the country is passing through a decisive phase in which protecting the Constitution and democracy is no longer merely a political issue, but a question concerning the future of the nation. “Intoxicated by its arrogance of power, the BJP government is undermining democratic conventions, the independence of constitutional institutions and the voting rights of citizens. Elections are the greatest expression of democracy. However, when serious questions are raised about the integrity of electoral rolls, complaints emerge regarding the deletion of voters’ names and doubts arise over the transparency of the electoral process, it signals a grave threat to the entire democratic framework.”

Mr. Hooda said that any attack on the Constitution is a direct attack on the country’s democratic framework and the rights of its citizens. “The Congress Party will continue its struggle, both on the streets and inside legislatures, to safeguard the Constitution, the independence of constitutional institutions and free and fair elections,” he said.
The HPCC president said “The anti-people policies and the BJP Government’s attitude towards democratic institutions have generated widespread public resentment.”

articles.title: Leave aside any differences, remove BJP in U.P., says Congress chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk; we have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power,’ said Mallikarjun Kharge

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday (November 26, 2026) in Lucknow urged party leaders and workers to strengthen the Samajwadi Party (SP)-Congress alliance and leave aside any differences in a bid to oust the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh. “To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk. We have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power. Narendra Modi and Gyanesh Kumar are forming an alliance and snatching the right to vote from the people through Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and EVM manipulation,” said Mr. Kharge, addressing a Constitution Day event at the State Congress office in Lucknow.

Highlighting the contribution of the grand old party in the freedom struggle and the deepening of India’s democracy, Mr. Kharge added, “Congress is a party that works together with everyone. It is the result of this collective effort that every citizen of the country has the right to vote today. We fought to save Baba Saheb’s Constitution and our rights through voting in 2024. This time too, if we work unitedly, we will definitely win”.

Hitting out at Union Home Minister Amit Shah over allegedly disrespecting Dr. B.R. articles.title: Delhi HC sets aside Centre’s order cancelling FCRA licence of NGO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,’ Justice A.J. Bhambhani said

The Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set aside the Centre’s order cancelling the FCRA licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC), holding that the allegation of the organisation engaging in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was unsupported by any material.
Editorial | Troubling bill: On the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026

“Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,” Justice A.J. Bhambhani said.

The judge added, “The respondent’s allegation that the appellant has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism”, is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation”.
Editorial | ​Fear of the foreign: On the FCRA amendments

The court further opined that the October 17, 2022 cancellation order the organisation’s FCRA registration was “misconceived, untenable and illegal, apart from being disproportionate and excessive in its rigour and impact”.

The court passed the judgment on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the October 2022 order of the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate.
The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country.
Editorial | Onerous rules: On the amended FCRA Rules, the fallout

The high court said the violations alleged in the cancellation order principally arise from the conditions for grant of an FCRA registration certificate, the essence of the allegation being that the NGO is guilty of diversion or misutilisation of such funds, or of using such funds for personal gains or diverting them for undesirable purposes.

articles.title: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098.

Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help!

Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer.

With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.

The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 27 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098.

Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help!

Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer.

With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.

The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

articles.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and Deputy Secretary of State, has died
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev

Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as Deputy Secretary of State under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday (November 26, 2026). He was 80.
His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he passed away peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home.

The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Mr. Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, who was ousted in 1964.
Talbott did, and it gave him some notoriety as a young man and a job at the magazine.

After 21 years at Time , where he focused on Soviet-American relations and held positions including Washington bureau chief and a foreign-affairs columnist, according to his US State Department biography, he received a call from the newly elected Clinton.
Then-Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in conversation with visiting then-U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbot, in New Delhi on April 08, 1994. | Photo Credit: UNI

Talbott joined the U.S. State Department in 1994, swiftly becoming Deputy Secretary of State. In that role, he was the architect of the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the US and India after the latter's nuclear tests in 1998.
Afterward, he served as the president of Brookings from 2002 to 2017. In that time, he also chaired the U.S. State Department's Foreign Affairs Policy Board.
Talbott also authored over a dozen books. His last book was titled “Our Founders' Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump,” which was published in 2020.

He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946, and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian; stepdaughter Rebecca Ascher-Walsh; siblings Kirk, Marjo and Page Talbott; and eight grandchildren, according to the New York Times.

articles.title: Mercury in cosmetics: What does the Keralam case reveal about health risks of skin-lightening creams | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: What does the recent case in Keralam reveal about mercury poisoning from cosmetics? How does exposure affect the kidneys, and what safeguards are in place to regulate unsafe products?

The quest for beauty and the enduring appeal for fair and blemishfree skin goes back to ages and across cultures. However, in recent years, this has been landing people in hospitals with serious health issues, as it happened in the case of the 17-year-old girl from Areekode in Malappuram district in Keralam.

Persuaded by many social influencers who raved about a face cream which gave them fair, blemishfree skin, she had also been using the same for over a year. The product with the brand name F-TUNES - claimed to contain turmeric and other “natural ingredients” and cited Dubai as the place of manufacture. She was hospitalised after she developed severe symptoms like fainting spells, swelling on legs and fall in blood pressure and was diagnosed with Membranous nephropathy, a condition wherein the immune system gets dysregulated, triggering nephrotic syndrome (heavy loss of protein through urine). Doctors traced her condition to the heavy mercury content in the face cream she was using. Lab analysis of a sample of the skin lightning cream obtained from the patient revealed that the product contained 12,500 ppm of mercury, way over the legal limit of 1 ppm

After prolonged treatment, the girl is now recovering. The police and drug regulatory authorities have begun a crackdown on the dubious cosmetic products in the market . The Health Minister has also threatened action against social influencers who are peddling dubious cosmetics online

Mercury is a highly toxic heavy metal and it can inhibit tyrosinase, a key enzyme produced by skin cells to produce melanin, the natural pigment that gives colour to skin and hair. The mercury in the face cream stops the production of new melanin and thins out the skin, giving it a lightening effect. The higher the content of mercury, the more spectacular the lightening effect, which consumers perceive as the product’s effectiveness.

articles.title: Kallakurichi MLA-woman IAS officer harassment case in Tamil Nadu: a timeline
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Here’s a timeline of how the Kallakurichi MLA-IAS officer row in Tamil Nadu unfolded, the Opposition’s charges and more

Tamil Nadu’s Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh has been at the centre of a political storm after he was accused of and booked on charges of misbehaving with a woman IAS officer. However, Mr. Vignesh, an MLA of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu , denied the charges earlier this month (November 2026).

It is alleged that the TVK MLA Arul Vignesh sent an inappropriate message to the woman IAS officer and behaved in an indecent manner under the influence of alcohol at her official residence. The issue first surfaced on social media.

Here’s a timeline of how the Kallakurichi MLA-woman IAS officer row unfolded, the allegations against the TVK legislator, the Opposition’s charges and more about the case that has stirred controversy in a major embarrassment for Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay-led TVK government that has come to power for the first time.

November 9, 2026 — DMK Parliamentary Party leader Kanimozhi Karunanidhi puts up a post on X, pointing out claims on social media that the TVK MLA had sent an inappropriate message to the officer and had visited her residence in an inebriated state. She demands a response from the TVK president and Chief Minister Mr. Vijay on the issue.

November 10, 2026 — Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh denies the charges and insists that the allegations made against him on social media were part of the “dirty politics” played by the Opposition. “I have always maintained high respect for government officers. articles.title: No need for CBI probe in Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Thirumavalavan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu government is taking appropriate legal action, says VCK leader

Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) founder Thol. Thirumavalavan on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said there was no need for a CBI probe into the allegations that the Kallakurichi TVK MLA had sent inappropriate messages to a District Collector. He said the Tamil Nadu government was taking appropriate legal action.

Speaking to journalists at Chennai, he said the VCK had consistently maintained that strict action should be taken against the MLA if he had sent messages to the Collector in a manner that caused mental distress.

“We have now received confirmation that a District Collector has formally lodged a complaint. Following this, the government has acted swiftly, registered a case against the particular MLA and initiated an investigation . We do not see any need for the CBI to intervene at this stage,” he said.

Responding to questions about the alleged delay in taking action, with 116 days having elapsed since the incident, Mr. Thirumavalavan said it was important to distinguish between the date of the alleged incident and the date on which the formal complaint was lodged.

“The incident came to light through the media and social media. The information available to us is that the Collector lodged a formal complaint only recently . We also learnt through social media reports that, when the incident occurred, she had not submitted a written complaint but had sought that the MLA be called and warned,” he contended.

He was responding to allegations that the Collector had earlier brought the matter to the attention of the Chief Secretary, who had allegedly attempted to persuade her to seek a transfer to another district. Opposition parties have cited the alleged delay and the handling of the complaint as reasons for seeking a CBI probe.

“Now that she has come forward and lodged a complaint, I believe the government is acting swiftly. A case has been registered under the appropriate sections, and I am confident that legal action will follow,” Mr. Thirumavalavan said.

articles.title: Bangladesh’s Opposition party blasts Australian media reports over leader’s visit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The party said the legal notice sent to The Australian newspaper pointed out ‘seven defamatory imputations and demands corrections, retraction of the report, an apology and the preservation of relevant documents’

Bangladesh’s main Opposition party, Jamaat-e-Islami, has sent a legal notice to a major Australian newspaper for publishing a report against its party chief, who has returned from the country, cutting short his overseas tour amid a controversy over his visit.

In a statement, the party late on Thursday (November 28, 2026) said the legal notice sent to The Australian newspaper pointed out “seven defamatory imputations and demands corrections, retraction of the report, an apology and the preservation of relevant documents” involving Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman’s tour.

“The publisher has been asked to provide a written response within 48 hours,” the statement said but did not explain what measure the party would take if the news outlet did not comply with the demand.

The report by The Australian described Mr. Rahman as a "Hamas-praising Bangladesh Islamist leader" and criticised the Australian government for allowing him into the country without stricter visa screening.
The Jamaat firmly rejected the report and said Mr. Rahman's early return was due to pressing organisational commitments in Bangladesh.
The Jamaat chief reached Sydney on November 20 as part of a weeklong overseas tour to Australia and Malaysia.
In Australia, he was scheduled to hold meetings with senior Australian government officials in Canberra and join receptions and community gatherings.

But a major media and diplomatic controversy erupted on November 23 when The Australian published a report titled “Sinwar was a hero': Fury as Hamas-praising Bangladesh Islamist leader arrives. articles.title: Major storm batters U.S. on Thanksgiving holiday; 400 flights cancelled
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history

A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history.
Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor’easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods.

As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage.
At airports, nearly 400 flights were canceled and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed.

New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday (November 28, 2026) due to what organizers said was an “abundance of caution.”

Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was canceled for three years during World War II.

Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious.

“While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss.
While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes.
Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption.

articles.title: President Donald Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet, before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) that he had seen sufficient information that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a security threat, while touting his administration’s intervention to save the scandal-plagued CEO’s job as “a great thing” for the world.
“I think he’s absolutely fine,” Mr. Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate.

Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation into Mr. Huang, Mr. Trump said his belief was based on “information I have, which is a lot of information.”
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return brings open-weight AI debate to forefront in Washington
Jensen Huang won’t need a pardon, says U.S. Vice President, as scrutiny of Nvidia scandal builds in Washington

Mr. Huang, a key figure in the AI revolution, was forced to resign earlier this month after revelations that he had an affair with a business executive who reportedly has ties to Chinese intelligence and whose company may have helped China obtain advanced chips in violation of U.S. export controls.
His sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet , before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound .

Mr. Trump revealed that he and other officials in his administration have worked behind the scenes to push for Huang to be reinstated, in a highly unusual intervention by the government into a top company’s decision making.
“I just thought, I saw that what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock, and I think it’s a great thing that he’s going back,” Mr. Trump said.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula appoints private banker as Finance Minister
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has appointed private banking executive Luiz Carlos Trabuco as Finance Minister for his next term, the presidency said on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
Mr. Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly.
The appointment of Mr. Trabuco, chairman of the board of Bradesco bank, aims to reassure the business community in Latin America’s largest economy.

“Luiz Carlos Trabuco has accepted President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s invitation to take the helm of the finance ministry,” the presidency stated, specifying that the banker agreed to take the job during an afternoon meeting with the Brazilian leader.
Mr. Lula will begin his fourth non-consecutive term in office in January and has so far only named one minister for that mandate.
Ahead of the official announcement, rumors circulating about Mr. Trabuco’s new job appeared to restore market confidence.
The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange was up 6% at closing on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
The national currency meanwhile regained strength after briefly crossing the symbolic threshold of six reais to the dollar on Monday.

articles.title: Apple pulls MiniMax AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: China cracked down on domestic AI companion apps including Xingye, banning intimate ⁠relationships for minors and ordering platforms to develop strict guardrails
Apple this ‌week removed MiniMax’s popular chatbot app Talkie from its App Store worldwide ​after media reports alleged that the product’s AI-generated characters sent ⁠sexualised messages to minors.
Launched in 2023, Talkie offers a wide array of companions for users to chat with, often with romantic undertones. Shanghai-based MiniMax also has a Chinese version ‌called Xingye.
ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism on Wednesday reported the app’s characters had sent sexually inappropriate and abusive ‌messages to children.

The app has an 18+ rating on both the ‌Apple ⁠App Store and Google Play Store and depending on the ⁠country, the app says children aged under 14 or under 16 cannot sign up. But child safety advocates have criticised its lax verification safeguards, which allow users to self-report their age.
MiniMax ​and Apple did not immediately ‌respond to requests for comment.
Talkie is offered in a range of languages and is particularly popular in the U.S., the Philippines and Mexico according to research firm Sensor Tower.

Unlike AI assistants commonly found on large language ‌models like ChatGPT or Gemini, AI companions are designed for sustained emotional ​engagement and human-like interactions with users, some with immersive storylines.
Talkie and Xingye have been big revenue drivers for MiniMax, contributing ⁠over 60% of its income in 2024. The company stopped breaking out chatbot-related revenue shares this year.
Talkie had roughly 11 million monthly active users across its ‌app and website as of October 2026, according to Chinese research firm Unique.
MiniMax has shifted its focus to enterprise coding and multimodal AI models such as MiniMax M1 and Hailuo-02, especially after its Hong Kong IPO in January.

articles.title: Prototype of Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX rover unveiled
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Chandrayaan-5/LuPEX mission is the fifth mission in the Chandrayaan series of lunar missions; JAXA, the Japanese space agency, unveiled the rover in Japan on November 25
The Japanese Space Agency, JAXA, has unveiled the prototype of the rover for the Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX (LUnar Polar EXploration) mission.

The Chandrayaan-5/LuPEX mission is the fifth mission in the Chandrayaan series of lunar missions to study the lunar volatile materials, including lunar water, in the vicinity of a Permanently Shadowed Region in the lunar South pole.
The JAXA unveiled the rover at the Chofu Aerospace Centre in Japan on November 25 and conducted a test demonstration.
The mission, which is scheduled to be launched in 2028 by the Japanese H3-24L launch vehicle, is a joint collaboration between the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the JAXA.
🌕️JAXA調布航空宇宙センターでの走行試験映像をたっぷりお届けします！ こちらの動画をご利用の際には以下のJDAのご利用方法を参照ください☺️ https://t.co/iKvpw12FrY https://t.co/Lb4x45zNA0
While the rover will be developed by the JAXA, the ISRO will be developing the lunar lander and will also be developing a few scientific instruments for the mission.

“The scientific instruments for this mission would be contributed by the ISRO, JAXA, European Space Agency (ESA) and National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), all thematically connected with the exploration and in-situ analysis of the volatiles reserved in the lunar polar region,” the ISRO had earlier said.
The NASA’s Neutron Spectrometer (NS) will also be onboard the rover, and according to the Japanese space agency, it is a neutron detector designed to search for water beneath the lunar surface.
Similarly, the ESA’s Exploration Mass Spectrometer for LUPEX (EMS-L) will also be part of the mission.
The ESA said that the EMS-L would investigate the moon’s extremely thin exosphere, a tenuous mist of atoms and molecules surrounding the lunar surface.

A seed-grown tree can live for 150 to 200 years. It is indeed very special,” he says.

Jayan, better known as Plavu Jayan (plavu is jackfruit in Malayalam), from Irinjalakkuda, Thrissur, is the recipient of the 29th PV Thampy Memorial Award 2026 for his tireless contribution to the conservation of jackfruit through the traditional method of planting.

It is a bond that goes back to his childhood, says the 61-year-old Jayan. “The jackfruit was an integral part of agrarian economy in our villages. The jackfruit was everywhere, it was an inevitable part of our lives. My mother’s family had a farming background, so my interest in jackfruit grew,” says Jayan.

The moniker Plavu Jayan came much ahead of his tree planting days. “I was 13 years old when, during Service Week in school, we were asked to get saplings. articles.title: Pint of View Kochi lectures explore Keralam’s unique socio-cultural identity
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The lecture series brings the State’s historical, cultural and environmental narratives into an informal bar setting

A lecture is in progress on the warmly lit terrace bar of Niko Hotels in Kadavathra. The audience, sipping on drinks, listens in rapt attention to accomplished herpetologist Sandeep Das as he talks about a very special amphibian — the Indian purple frog. Research Associate, Department of Biotechnology, Government of India and Member of Kerala State Wildlife Board, Sandeep has been studying the ancient frog species for 15 years and shares his insights on its peculiar life and behaviour.

At the end of the session, a number of questions emerge from the audience and a lively discussion ensues. This is the Kochi chapter of Pint of View, a lecture movement that has taken over bars and pubs across the country, converting them into temporary learning hubs.
A Pint of View lecture | Photo Credit: Akkshay Lawrence
A movement that was launched in Bengaluru in 2025 by Harsh Snehanshu, Shruti Sah, and Meghna Chaudhary, it caught on in India, with a presence in over 16 cities now.

The Kochi chapter, launched in September, has hosted six lectures to enthusiastic crowds. Kochi curators Krupa Anilkumar and Kurien Philip are delighted with the response from the people and say the idea is to make knowledge accessible to the public in a fun way. “Many of us stop learning after we leave college. Though the desire to learn is present, we may still be carrying the trauma of competitive classroom environments. And that is where these lectures change the game. Hosted at bars and pubs, people are easily relaxed and therefore more receptive to new information and ways of thinking,” she says.
A Pint of View session in progress | Photo Credit: Akkshay Lawrence

The lectures so far reflect the historical, socio-cultural and environmental uniqueness of Keralam. The inaugural lecture was on 50 years of Kochi, by Johanne Binny Kuruvilla, founder of the Kochi Heritage Project, where he spoke about the unique modernity of Kochi — how it emerged and existed as a revolutionary space. “Intended for adults, the audience that we find here are largely working professionals, who are driven by the curiosity to learn. We have many regular attendees,” says Kurien.

The speakers are often senior academicians. But that does not exclude those with expertise in a subject. Musician, composer and co-founder of the performance collective, Oorali, Saji Oorali’s session explored the connection between spice trade and the music of Keralam. From the maappila paattu, which has traces of Arab influence, owing to the traders who visited the Malabar coast to European church music that introduced new instruments and traditions to South India and Malayalam hip-hop finding audiences around the world, the session was a glimpse into the history of Keralam’s music. The session also included live musical demonstrations.

Urban and ecological anthropologist, Mathew A Varghese, who is an assistant professor, School of International Relations and Politics, Mahatma Gandhi University, in his lecture, ‘The City Unfolding’ reflected on how Keralam’s urban spaces are designed, how they have transformed and how people experience and make sense of the places their inhabit.
For now, the lectures are hosted at Niko, Rocks and Brews and Vasco’s Corner.

articles.title: Polavaram evacuees boycott panchayat polls in Eluru district, demand separate panchayat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Families resettled at Koruturu R&R Colony also stayed away from the MPTC and ZPTC elections earlier this month

Families displaced by the Polavaram irrigation project, who have been shifted to the Resettlement and Rehabilitation (R&R) Colony at Koruturu village in Jeelugumilli mandal of Eluru district, boycotted the gram panchayat elections on Thursday (November 26, 2026), demanding a separate panchayat for them.
The Polavaram project evacuees, who fall under P. Ankampalem panchayat, also boycotted the MPTC and ZPTC elections held on November 6.

The government shifted many families from Tekuru, Gajulagondi, Sirivaka and Chiduru habitations to the R&R Colony at Koruturu a few years ago. Since then, the project-displaced families have been demanding that the government constitute a separate panchayatand provide them with the necessary amenities.
According to sources, Polavaram, Jeelugumilli, Buttaigudem and Velerupadu mandals in the Agency area of Eluru district have more than 1.18 lakh voters.
“The election officers held discussions with the voters in Jeelugumilli, but failed to convince them to exercise their franchise,” an officer said.

The polling staff waited at the polling booths from 7 a.m. to 1 p.m., but the villagers refused to cast their votes. They insisted that the government must consider their demand, a poll official said.
“The demand for a separate panchayat has been taken to the notice of the authorities concerned,” an officer said.

articles.title: DMK sets conditions to support Delimitation Bill
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu’s share in Lok Sabha should not be reduced and the existing proportional strength of all States as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census must remain frozen for another 25 years, are Mr. Stalin’s two demands for supporting the Delimitation bill

In the Narendra Modi government’s fresh bid to pass the Delimitation Bills, the support of 22 Lok Sabha members from Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) is crucial to achieve the required two-third majority, which it had failed to get in the bill’s last outing in April.

DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, on Friday (November 27, 2026) asserted that there would be no “compromise” with Tamil Nadu’s interests. The DMK has set out two conditions for supporting the Delimitation Bill: Tamil Nadu’s existing share of seats in the Lok Sabha should be maintained, and the existing proportional strength of all States, as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census, must remain frozen for another 25 years.
Political & National Report: DMK sets conditions to support Delimitation Bill. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Atchannaidu orders Statewide inspection of fishing boats, warns officials of action over lapses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nearly 80% of the State’s fishing boats have been fitted with transponders, the Minister says, asking officials to cover the rest quickly

Andhra Pradesh Agriculture and Fisheries Minister Kinjarapu Atchannaidu has warned officials of stringent action if lapses in enforcing safety measures lead to the loss of fishermen’s lives, ordering a Statewide inspection of fishing boats to check their fitness and safety equipment.

Reviewing safety measures, installation of transponders, boat fitness and insurance coverage at his camp office in Vijayawada on Friday (November 27, 2026), the Minister directed officials to ensure strict compliance with safety regulations.

Expressing concern over fishermen venturing into the sea despite cyclone warnings issued by the Fisheries Department, the Disaster Management Department and the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS), he said even experienced fishermen should not underestimate natural disasters and must follow the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) during both routine fishing trips and cyclones.

Mr. Atchannaidu said nearly 80% of fishing boats in the State had been fitted with transponders and directed Fisheries Commissioner Rama Shankar Naik to expedite installation in the remaining boats. Officials should educate fishermen on using the devices during emergencies and regularly check their functioning, he said. Defective equipment should be repaired or replaced immediately.

He ordered comprehensive inspections of fishing boats along the State’s coastline to assess their fitness and safety equipment. A detailed report should be prepared on the number of boats fitted with transponders, those yet to be covered and the reasons for delays.

Fishermen should contact the Fisheries Development Officer (FDO), Fisheries Inspector or Village Fisheries Assistant (VFA) if they encounter technical problems. Officials must respond promptly to complaints, he said.

The Minister directed officials to bring every eligible fisherman under insurance schemes implemented by the State government and the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB). Eligible workers engaged in fish and shrimp farms, the feed sector and allied fisheries activities should also receive insurance benefits as per scheme guidelines.

He warned that officials responsible for depriving eligible fishermen of insurance benefits through negligence would face departmental action. Recovery of the lost amount from those responsible could also be considered as per rules.

The Commissioner was asked to convene a special Statewide review and monitor implementation of safety measures. Mr. Atchannaidu said human errors and official negligence resulting in loss of life would not be tolerated and called on fishermen to heed safety warnings.

Expressing concern over fishermen venturing into the sea despite cyclone warnings issued by the Fisheries Department, the Disaster Management Department and the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS), he said even experienced fishermen should not underestimate natural disasters and must follow the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) during both routine fishing trips and cyclones.

Officials should educate fishermen on using the devices during emergencies and regularly check their functioning, he said. Defective equipment should be repaired or replaced immediately.

He ordered comprehensive inspections of fishing boats along the State’s coastline to assess their fitness and safety equipment. A detailed report should be prepared on the number of boats fitted with transponders, those yet to be covered and the reasons for delays.

Fishermen should contact the Fisheries Development Officer (FDO), Fisheries Inspector or Village Fisheries Assistant (VFA) if they encounter technical problems. Officials must respond promptly to complaints, he said.

The Minister directed officials to bring every eligible fisherman under insurance schemes implemented by the State government and the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB). Eligible workers engaged in fish and shrimp farms, the feed sector and allied fisheries activities should also receive insurance benefits as per scheme guidelines.

He warned that officials responsible for depriving eligible fishermen of insurance benefits through negligence would face departmental action. Recovery of the lost amount from those responsible could also be considered as per rules.

The Commissioner was asked to convene a special Statewide review and monitor implementation of safety measures. Mr. Atchannaidu said human errors and official negligence resulting in loss of life would not be tolerated and called on fishermen to heed safety warnings.
