articles.title: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court

The Supreme Court indicated orally on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) its inclination to set aside a Calcutta High Court order that put on hold the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections over a delimitation exercise, and requested the High Court to hear the dispute afresh.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the suggestion while hearing an appeal filed by the West Bengal government against the High Court order of November 6. The High Court had directed the West Bengal State Election Commission to not notify the elections until a petition challenging the delimitation of municipal wards was decided.

Chief Justice Kant said the apex court was inclined to set aside the order of the High Court after taking into consideration pertinent legal and factual issues raised by the State government. The writ petition could also be transferred from the Single Judge Bench to a Division Bench, which would consider the entire dispute afresh and pass appropriate orders.
“And till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off,” the court suggested orally.

The lawyers for both the State and former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das, who had filed the petition in the High Court against the delimitation exercise, sought time to take instructions. The court listed the case for further hearing on November 30.
The Bench reasoned that its proposed “ad-hoc arrangement” would place both parties on an “even keel” without the Supreme Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the dispute.
The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144.

A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise.

Mr. Das had questioned the delimitation, arguing that the expansion of the municipal wards was void. He had sought a quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards as bad in law. He had contended that the delimitation happened on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, resulting in the alleged exclusion of a substantial number of residents.
After the Single Judge Bench had refused his pleas for an interim stay of the elections, Mr. Das had moved the High Court’s Division Bench.

articles.title: Governor seeks CM’s report on compliance with SC’s directions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam.

The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipilliyar Temple — on Tuesday, defying the Supreme Court’s direction to light it on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement”.

Sources told The Hindu that the Governor had sought a report from the Chief Minister under Article 167(b) of the Constitution, detailing the action taken by the authorities on the Supreme Court’s directions.

It came on the heels of the Madurai Collector telling the Supreme Court, in a preliminary status report filed on Wednesday, that he had made every arrangement to comply with the court’s November 20 order to light the lamp on the deepathoon , but the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniyaswamy Temple had failed to authorise a lamp-lighting team.

Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam.

The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipilliyar Temple — on Tuesday, defying the Supreme Court’s direction to light it on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement”.

articles.title: Rajbanshi language to be included in Eighth Schedule of Constitution: Suvendu Adhikari
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This was a promise made the BJP during their 2026 Assembly election campaign

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that the Rajbanshi language will be included in the Eight Schedule of the Constitution, a promise that their party had made during their Assembly election campaign.

During the inauguration of a festival in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district, Mr Adhikari said that their government is taking complete care of the Rajbanshi community, including their language, culture, political aspirations, and financial security.

He added that as promised in BJP’s West Bengal Assembly poll manifesto and reiterated by several top BJP leaders during the buildup to the elections, Rajbanshi language is set to be part of the Eight Schedule of the Constitution.

“We raised the issue during a meeting with the Union home minister and the home secretary on November 19 that was attended by me and the state’s chief secretary,” Mr Adhikari told reporters before the inauguration of Ras Utsav (annual celebration of Radha-Krishna) festivities in Cooch Behar.

At Cooch Behar, Mr Adhikari was greeted by Cabinet minister Nisith Pramanik, a member of the Rajbanshi community. Later, the CM also took part in the festivities in the local area. Mr Adhikari also added that the Rajbanshi community expressed their dissatisfaction over losing their land ownership in the region as he held the Left Front government responsible for it.

He also added that the previous governments in the State did not offer much participation of the Rajbanshi community in the cabinet and that their government has done more for the community since they came to power. The Rajbanshi community has always stood by us since 2019, Mr Adhikari added. In the recently concluded assembly polls, the BJP performed exceptionally well in north Bengal and won eight out of nine seats in the Cooch Behar district.

articles.title: Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In his memorandum to Chairperson of Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram MP, Thol. Thirumavalavan said, “the right to choose one’s partner is not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community” but “an aspect of the constitutional freedom and dignity of every individual”.

In his request to the Commission headed by Justice K.N. Basha, Mr. Thirumavalavan said that the Commission should “recommend the enactment of a comprehensive Tamil Nadu law against honour killings and honour-based crimes, with a broad definition rooted in the right to choose a partner and individual autonomy”.

He further urged the Commission to provide a framework to address “collective and mob-based honour violence”, which would ensure that “every person who intentionally participates in, instigates, facilitates or enables the crime can be held accountable under clearly defined standards of criminal responsibility”.

The VCK leader further said that enforceable duties and penalties should be imposed on police and public officials who fail to protect couples despite credible threats, including wilful refusal to register complaints, disclosure of confidential information and dereliction of preventive duties.

Mr. Thirumavalavan also demanded that there exist comprehensive protection for couples, survivors, witnesses and their families, including safehouses, relocation, legal aid, counselling, medical care, compensation and rehabilitation. He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.

articles.title: No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: People Against SIR emailed the police details of the proposed Constitution Day march from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar; the police, however, say they have received no such communication and warn that Section 163 of BNSS remains in force in the area

No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls , scheduled for November 26 , senior New Delhi police officials said. The organisers, however, maintained that they had intimated the police about the proposed demonstration.

The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform has called for a march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg towards Jantar Mantar. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated site for peaceful protests, among other demands.

An email dated November 23, 2026, seen by The Hindu , was sent to the Delhi Police to inform them about the proposed programme. It stated: “This is to inform you that we, the Delhi People Against SIR, are going to observe Constitution Day as per the details given.”

The email further stated that participants would assemble outside Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg at 12.30 p.m. on November 26 and march towards Jantar Mantar via Kali Bari Marg. “This is for your information and any follow-up/arrangements,” it added.
“We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march,” Maimoona Mollah, a representative of the platform, told The Hindu .

Ms. Mollah claimed that the police had acknowledged the intimation and subsequently sought further details, including the proposed route and the expected number of participants expected. These details, she said, were shared with the police over a telephone conversation. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration.

Public notice 🔶Information has been received that Samyukta Kisan Morcha and other activists are planning a protest march from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar on 26.11.2026. No application for permission has been received and no permission has been granted for the said march. 🔶Section 163 BNSS, 2023, is in force in New Delhi District. Unauthorised gatherings, processions, demonstrations, speeches, sloganeering and dharnas are prohibited. 🔶All are requested to comply with the order u/s 163 BNSS and cooperate with Police. Violations will invite legal action.

However, New Delhi police officers denied receiving the intimation and stressed that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remain in force in the area and warned that action would be taken against gatherings in violation of the restrictions.

The police said “preventive” security measures would be put in place to prevent any unauthorised gathering in the area. These would include multi-layer barricading, deployment of additional personnel and preventive detentions, if required, to disperse crowds and prevent protesters from assembling in violation of the prohibitory orders.

People Against SIR was formed on October 14 following an emergency consultation in Delhi attended by representatives of more than 200 organisations. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18 States to campaign against the SIR exercise.

articles.title: Uttariya instead of robes: West Bengal Government suggests universities to adopt Indian attire in convocations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay said that the government was putting effort to follow own Indian culture and tradition and Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies

West Bengal Higher Education Department has advised all the State-aided universities to adopt Indian attire such as Uttariya and clothes made of handloom fabric instead of Western robes during convocation or any academic ceremony.

“We are putting effort to follow our own Indian culture and tradition. Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies. Why do we have to wear robes? Many institutions, including the Indian Institute of Technology [IIT], have adopted only uttariya. Hence, we made the suggestion,” West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay told media persons on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

The development also came days after Mr. Chattopadhyay praised the Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College for upholding Indian traditions by replacing the conventional academic gown with a traditional uttariya.
“As we strive to build a self-reliant Bharat, our education system must also reflect our civilisational values and cultural identity,” he wrote on X congratulating the students of the college.
In its notice sent to all the vice chancellors of the universities, the department has now said that the UGC had not prescribed any rigid uniform design for ceremonial robes.
Hence, the universities have the flexibility to incorporate traditional Indian attire, such as the uttariya, and to design distinct ceremonial attire for dignitaries and degree recipients.

Monday’s (November 23) notice to the VCs said that the ceremonial attire made from Indian handloom was more suited to India’s climate. Such a preference for handloom fabrics and traditional Indian attire also supports the rural handloom industry and weavers’ livelihoods, it said.

“In view of the above, you are requested to take necessary steps to consider adopting handloom fabrics and traditional attire for the academic robes worn during convocation in your esteemed university as well as affiliated colleges, wherever applicable,” the department stated in the advisory asking the universities to send to confirmation of the communication to the department.

articles.title: Congress wins majority of Zila Pramukh posts in Rajasthan polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The votes for panchayat samitis and zila parishads were counted on November 20 in 37 of the State’s 41 districts

After its decisive victory in the last week’s Panchayati Raj elections, the Opposition Congress in Rajasthan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) took control of 24 of the 37 zila parishads which elected their heads, while the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party secured 10 Zila Pramukh posts despite having a majority in just five rural district bodies.

The Bharat Adivasi Party won tribal-dominated Banswara and Dungarpur, while Nagaur MP Hanuman Beniwal’s Rashtriya Loktantrik Party retained Nagaur. No independent candidate was elected Zila Pramukh in any district.

The votes for panchayat samitis and zila parishads were counted on November 20 in 37 of the State’s 41 districts. Members elected in the panchayat polls voted on Wednesday to choose their respective heads, while the results in the remaining four districts – Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sriganganagar – will be declared in December.

The BJP pulled off a surprise victory in Churu, where the Congress had a clear majority, and secured five of the eight zila parishads where no party had an absolute majority. The Congress largely managed to keep its flock together, losing only one of the 23 rural bodies where it enjoyed majority.

Congress candidate Mamta Gurjar defeated BJP’s Nirmala Rawat by just one vote in Beawar, despite the BJP having a majority. Renu Wala of Congress defeated BJP’s Pooja Jatav by 17 votes to 14 in Bharatpur, which is Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma’s home district.

Among the zila parishads where no party had a clear majority, the BJP won Balotra, Didwana-Kuchaman, Deeg, Khairthal-Tijara and Pratapgarh, and the Congress won Salumbar. In Churu, where the Congress held 21 of the 39 seats against the BJP’s 17, ruling party candidate Kanika Singh, daughter-in-law of former Minister Rajendra Rathore, defeated Congress candidate Prakash Devi, indicating cross-voting.

Congress candidate Nikita Dudi defeated party rebel Sarita Choudhary, who contested as an Independent, by 23 votes to 18 in Bikaner. Dissatisfaction over the party nomination had reportedly led to the rebellion, while the BJP had withdrawn its candidate in Bikaner.

The Congress narrowly avoided an embarrassment in Dholpur despite holding 21 of the 29 seats, as its candidate Anisha Singh defeated her nearest rival by just one vote. The BJP also secured Balotra zila parishad by one vote. The Congress registered comfortable victories in several of its traditional strongholds, including Jaipur, Jodhpur, Alwar, Sikar and Bhilwara.

Twenty-one-year-old Congress candidate Santosh Kumari was elected unopposed as Zila Pramukh in Jaisalmer. Ms. Kumari, who completed her class XII and is unmarried, belongs to a Scheduled Tribe community. Two other candidates elected unopposed were Beena Bairwa in Dausa and Asha Devi in Sawai Madhopur. Both of them were Congress candidates.

There were stray incidents of arguments and jostling at some places during the election process. Tensions were reported in Jaipur, Bharatpur and Bhilwara, where workers and leaders of rival parties were involved in heated exchanges.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 26 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Congress wins majority of Zila Pramukh posts in Rajasthan polls

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The votes for panchayat samitis and zila parishads were counted on November 20 in 37 of the State’s 41 districts

After its decisive victory in the last week’s Panchayati Raj elections, the Opposition Congress in Rajasthan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) took control of 24 of the 37 zila parishads which elected their heads, while the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party secured 10 Zila Pramukh posts despite having a majority in just five rural district bodies.

The Bharat Adivasi Party won tribal-dominated Banswara and Dungarpur, while Nagaur MP Hanuman Beniwal’s Rashtriya Loktantrik Party retained Nagaur. No independent candidate was elected Zila Pramukh in any district.

The votes for panchayat samitis and zila parishads were counted on November 20 in 37 of the State’s 41 districts. Members elected in the panchayat polls voted on Wednesday to choose their respective heads, while the results in the remaining four districts – Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sriganganagar – will be declared in December.

The BJP pulled off a surprise victory in Churu, where the Congress had a clear majority, and secured five of the eight zila parishads where no party had an absolute majority. The Congress largely managed to keep its flock together, losing only one of the 23 rural bodies where it enjoyed majority.

Congress candidate Mamta Gurjar defeated BJP’s Nirmala Rawat by just one vote in Beawar, despite the BJP having a majority. Renu Wala of Congress defeated BJP’s Pooja Jatav by 17 votes to 14 in Bharatpur, which is Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma’s home district.

Among the zila parishads where no party had a clear majority, the BJP won Balotra, Didwana-Kuchaman, Deeg, Khairthal-Tijara and Pratapgarh, and the Congress won Salumbar. In Churu, where the Congress held 21 of the 39 seats against the BJP’s 17, ruling party candidate Kanika Singh, daughter-in-law of former Minister Rajendra Rathore, defeated Congress candidate Prakash Devi, indicating cross-voting.

Congress candidate Nikita Dudi defeated party rebel Sarita Choudhary, who contested as an Independent, by 23 votes to 18 in Bikaner. Dissatisfaction over the party nomination had reportedly led to the rebellion, while the BJP had withdrawn its candidate in Bikaner.

The Congress narrowly avoided an embarrassment in Dholpur despite holding 21 of the 29 seats, as its candidate Anisha Singh defeated her nearest rival by just one vote. The BJP also secured Balotra zila parishad by one vote. The Congress registered comfortable victories in several of its traditional strongholds, including Jaipur, Jodhpur, Alwar, Sikar and Bhilwara.

Twenty-one-year-old Congress candidate Santosh Kumari was elected unopposed as Zila Pramukh in Jaisalmer. Ms. Kumari, who completed her class XII and is unmarried, belongs to a Scheduled Tribe community. Two other candidates elected unopposed were Beena Bairwa in Dausa and Asha Devi in Sawai Madhopur. Both of them were Congress candidates.

There were stray incidents of arguments and jostling at some places during the election process. Tensions were reported in Jaipur, Bharatpur and Bhilwara, where workers and leaders of rival parties were involved in heated exchanges.

articles.title: Bihar cabinet approves 1294.37 acres of land for industrial areas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cabinet also approved dismissal of 11 government doctors from service. For the first time Cabinet meeting conducted through e-Cabinet system. Bihar Cabinet approved a total of 34 decisions.
The Bihar cabinet on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) approved the acquisition of 1294.37 acres of land for industrial areas in Nalanda, Samastipur, and Sheikhpura.

It approved ₹706.51 crore for the acquisition of 1294.37 acres of land for industrial use, Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary told reporters in a post cabinet briefing.
All these acquisitions will be carried out by Infrastructure Development Authority (IDA), Patna, he added.
A total of 34 decisions were taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.
In yet another decision, the cabinet gave its nod for constitution of “Bihar Economic Advisory Council” (BEAC) as a special advisory body to provide recommendations and advice to the Chief Minister.

The BEAC will be constituted on the lines of Economic Advisory Council (EAC) to the Prime Minister functions at the Centre, ACS said while explaining the functions of the Council that will include: recommending structural reforms in the state’s economy, formulating strategies for rapid, inclusive and broad-based economic growth, promoting economic stability, enhancing revenue generation and strengthening public finance.

Besides, undertaking any other tasks assigned by the Chief Minister from time to time. The role of the Council will be advisory in nature. It will consist of a maximum of five members, including its Chairperson who will be nominated by the state government. The Secretary (Expenditure), Finance Department, will serve as the ex-officio Secretary of the Council.

The cabinet also gave administrative approval of Rs 1,794.32 crore for the Patna Water Supply Project under the centrally sponsored AMRUT 2.0 Mission, Mr. Chaudhary said adding that this is a major step toward strengthening Patna’s water supply system.

The cabinet approved the health department’s proposal for dismissal of 11 government doctors. The dismissed doctors were posted across districts including Saharsa, Bhagalpur, Supaul, Banka and Madhepura.
These doctors were found absent from their place of posting for more than five years without giving information to the authorities concerned, Mr. Chaudhary said.

articles.title: Delhi High Court grants time to ED to respond to Engineer Rashid’s plea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice Sachin Datta listed the matter for further hearing on December 16 after the prosecutor said he needed one week to consult the special public prosecutor in the case

The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) granted time to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to respond to a plea by Baramulla MP Abdul Rashid Sheikh , challenging the framing of charges against him in a money laundering case linked to alleged funding from Pakistan through hawala channels for secessionist activities in Jammu and Kashmir.
Justice Sachin Datta listed the matter for further hearing on December 16 after the prosecutor said he needed one week to consult the special public prosecutor in the case.
Mr. Rashid Sheikh, also known as Engineer Rashid, has challenged a September 9 order by which the trial court had ordered the framing of charges against the people.

On October 24, the special court had formally framed charges against the accused and put them on trial under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) after finding sufficient material on record to raise a strong suspicion of their involvement in the offence.
The ED has alleged that proceeds of crime amounting to Rs 8.94 crore were generated and received, routed, transferred, concealed, possessed, acquired and used by the accused through various channels.

The seven accused include Malik, chief of the banned Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF), separatist leader Shabir Ahmad Shah, Masarat Alam, Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali, Naval Kishore Kapoor, and M/s Trison Farms and Constructions Pvt Ltd.

The ED case stems from a 2017 National Investigation Agency (NIA) case in which charges under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) were invoked.

The prosecution has alleged that the accused received funds from the “Pakistani establishment” through hawala channels and other means to propagate secessionist activities and carry out acts prejudicial to the law of the land.

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran , whose huge pop hits include “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “The Reflex” and “Rio” and whose rise up the charts was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

“From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
“I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band,” he wrote. “You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible.”

The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Music Award recipients.

Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesisers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people's walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heartthrobs and the band being labelled part of the New Romantics. fullParagraphs: The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor’s office said in a statement
A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), killing at least 30 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor's office said in a statement.
The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the Health Ministry.

At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video shows firefighters working to put out the fire spreading amongst the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.
Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The Public Prosecutor's office said DNA investigations were underway to identify the victims.

Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene himself. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further.

Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.
In January, 21 people were killed and 16 injured in a massive multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

articles.title: Constitution Day LIVE updates: Priceless heritage of Indian democracy, says PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress to hold ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches across states on Constitution Day, intensifying its campaign against alleged electoral roll manipulation and the ECI’s failure to safeguard the right to vote

On November 26, 2026, India marks 77 years since the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution in 1949. That founding charter made a bold promise for a poor, deeply stratified country emerging from colonial rule. Every adult citizen, regardless of property, caste, gender, or creed, would stand equal at the ballot box. Today, that core principle of political democracy, which B.R. Ambedkar placed at the heart of the Republic, is being systematically erased in practice.

Every November 26, on Constitution Day in India, a striking visual emerges on the political landscape. Opposition leaders, civil rights activists, and citizens step into the public space clutching pocket-sized editions of the Constitution of India — often bound in bright red. articles.title: Supreme Court issues notice on bail pleas by Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam in 2020 Delhi riots case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court declined to take up their pleas for interim relief; CJI to set up three-judge Bench to decide whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override stringent bail curbs under UAPA

The Supreme Court issued notice on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) on the bail pleas of former JNU scholar Umar Khalid and activist Sharjeel Imam, accused in the larger conspiracy case linked to the 2020 Delhi riots. The court, however, declined to take up their pleas for interim relief, saying a three-judge Bench would be set up to decide whether prolonged incarceration and delay in trial can override stringent bail curbs imposed by the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), 1967.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana sought the Delhi Police’s response to the bail pleas by December 14. It also directed the Registry to place the matter before the CJI on the administrative side for the constitution of a larger Bench in light of the court’s May 22 judgment in Tasleem Ahmed v. State Government of NCT of Delhi.

“Issue notice, returnable on 14.12.2026. The Registry is directed to put up the matter before Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India, on the administrative side, for constitution of a three-Judge Bench in light of the judgment dated 22.05.2026,” the Bench said.

The May 22 reference arose from divergent interpretations by coordinate Benches of the law governing bail under the UAPA. In its January 5 verdict, a Division Bench comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and P.B. Varale had granted bail to five other accused in the case but denied relief to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam on the ground that the roles attributed to them stood on a “qualitatively different footing”. The court permitted them to renew their bail pleas after a year or upon completion of the examination of protected witnesses, whichever was earlier.

Subsequently, on May 18, a Bench comprising Justices B. V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan, while granting bail to an accused in a narco-terrorism case, expressed reservations about the January 5 judgment, observing that it had failed to correctly apply the binding principles laid down in the court’s 2021 ruling in Union of India v. K. A. Najeeb. In Najeeb, the court had held that the stringent bail embargo under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA could “melt down” where prolonged incarceration and delay in trial infringed an accused’s fundamental rights.

Following this, Justices Kumar and Varale referred the matter to the CJI on May 22 for the constitution of a larger Bench to ensure “parity and consistency” in the application of binding precedents by coordinate Benches. The Bench, however, granted six months’ interim bail to Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi, two other accused in the conspiracy case, observing that they “cannot be made to suffer” merely because a question of law awaited authoritative settlement.

At the outset of Wednesday’s hearing, senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Siddhartha Dave, appearing for Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, respectively, urged the court to consider their pleas for interim bail, pointing out that both had been in custody for over six years. Mr. Dave argued that the prayer for interim relief was distinct from the larger question of law referred to the CJI on May 22.
“Only the main matter on the legal issue is under reference. Let the issue of interim come up for hearing,” Mr. Sibal submitted, seeking an early hearing.
The CJI, however, said he would have to first examine the conflicting interpretations of the Najeeb ruling, which he had authored.

“…in the light of the conflict of observation, I have to apply my mind. It was my judgment (Najeeb case) which is being discussed. So, I am feeling a little embarrassed. One bench says Najeeb means this; another bench says it does not mean… I am being told what I have said,” the CJI remarked.

“They have this mindset of paying Pakistan and get bomb thrown at the country,” said Mr. Ambedkar, alleging that BJP and RSS were returning to communal politics to win elections, with an agenda built on being “anti-Muslim and anti-Pakistan.”

articles.title: Keralam Minister announces ‘Speak up to stand up’ for woman survivors of violence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Beneficiaries will be provided with safe accommodation, counselling, social and emotional support, free legal aid, opportunities for continuing their education, employment, and skill training

Keralam Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) announced ‘Speak up to stand up,’ a scheme for ensuring comprehensive support and financial empowerment of woman survivors of violence to lead them towards independence.

Inaugurating the State-level observance of International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women at Government College for Women, Vazhuthacaud, Thiruvananthapuram, the Minister said the objective of the scheme was to create a Keralam where each girl and woman could walk without fear, study, work, and choose the life she wanted.

The initiative was a continuation of Kerala Police’s ‘Speak up’ scheme that aimed at rehabilitation and financial empowerment of woman survivors. Intended to help woman survivors rebuild their lives with confidence, ‘Speak up to stand up’ would be implemented with the support of the Women and Child Development (WCD) department, Kerala Women’s Commission, and Kerala State Women’s Development Corporation (KSWDC) Ltd.

The needs, interests, and skills of each survivor of violence will be analysed and individual rehabilitation plans prepared with their consent. They will be provided with safe accommodation, counselling, social and emotional support, free legal aid, opportunities for continuing their education, employment, and skill training.
Self-employment schemes of the KSWDC and Kudumbashree network mechanisms would also be tapped into to help women start own ventures and earn an income.
The emergency protection for the survivors and further services will be provided through the WCD’s women protection officers, 181 Mitra help line, and Sakhi one-stop centres.

The Minister took the occasion to remind the attendees that dowry was not a symbol of status or pride, but an illegal practice. Defamation through social media, misuse of private pictures and information, and cyber threats should also be taken seriously. “The youth should be ready to react to violence and question wrong practices,” Ms. Krishna said.
An art wall with the message of ‘Not silence, but reply,’ mime, and flash mob by students kicked off the day’s events. An interaction between the Minister and the students was also held.
Kerala Women’s Commission chairperson P. Satheedevi presided over the programme.

articles.title: India Pavilion bags Visitors’ Lion at Venice Biennale; PM Modi calls it ‘proud moment for country’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The pavilion, under the theme ‘Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home’, explored memory and belonging in a rapidly transforming world

The India Pavilion has won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the prestigious Venice Art Biennale, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the award as a “proud moment” for India’s art and cultural world.
The pavilion, under the theme ‘Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home’, explored memory and belonging in a rapidly transforming world.
Earlier in the day, Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat described it on X as a “remarkable recognition” of the country’s growing cultural influence.
A view of artist Skarma Sonam Tashi’s installation on display at India’s national pavilion at the 61st Venice Art Biennale, in Venice, Italy. Photo: X/@gssjodhpur via PTI.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the award as a “proud moment” for India’s art and cultural world.

“Delighted that the India Pavilion at the Venice Art Biennale has won the prestigious Visitors’ Lion for Best National Pavilion. Our artists are bringing fresh perspectives to the world of art, drawing inspiration from India’s rich and diverse cultural heritage. May this feat inspire many more young Indians to pursue art and explore new creative horizons,” he posted on X, while sharing Mr. Shekhawat’s post.
The biennale ran from May 9 to November 22, with previews from May 6-8.
The India Pavilion returned to the Biennale Arte — one of the components of La Biennale di Venezia — after a gap of seven years.
The pavilion was opened at the 61st International Art Exhibition at the Biennale, in Venice, in the presence of Shekhawat and other officials.

“A moment of immense pride! India wins the Best National Pavilion – Visitors’ Lion at the Venice Art Biennale, the Olympics of the art world. The honour, decided through votes by visitors from across the globe, is a remarkable recognition of India’s growing cultural influence,” Mr. Shekhawat said.

The India Pavilion has won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the prestigious Venice Art Biennale, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the award as a “proud moment” for India’s art and cultural world.

The pavilion, under the theme ‘Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home’, explored memory and belonging in a rapidly transforming world.

The biennale ran from May 9 to November 22, with previews from May 6-8.

The India Pavilion returned to the Biennale Arte — one of the components of La Biennale di Venezia — after a gap of seven years.

articles.title: Kallakurichi police serve summons on TVK MLA Arul Vignesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: An Inspector attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person

The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh in connection with a case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer.

Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Mr. Arul Vignesh at the house.

The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages.
FIR registered against Kallakurichi TVK MLA for ‘misbehaving’ with woman IAS officer, Madras High Court told
Udhayanidhi Stalin submits petition to Tamil Nadu DGP demanding arrest of Kallakurichi and Thuraiyur TVK MLAs
Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Internal Complaints Committee has been constituted, Madras High Court told
The police have booked a case against the MLA under four sections including the POSH Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita

Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case registered at the Kallakurichi All Women Police station, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday (November 25).
The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry.
Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the Kallakurichi All Women Police station and the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.

articles.title: U.S. announces new 25% tariffs on India, second-highest in the 14 countries against which action has been taken
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The order by the U.S. Trade Representative also opens the door for a lower 17% tariff if India and the U.S. sign a trade deal

The U.S. government on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) announced a tariff of 25% on goods imported from India in response to India’s “unreasonable acts, policies, and practices” that “burden or restrict U.S. commerce”. This is the second-highest tariff among the 14 economies against which the latest action has been taken, second only to the 35% tariff levied on Vietnam.

However, the order by the office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) also said that, should the U.S. and India reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, the tariff imposed on India could drop to 17%.
ALSO WATCH U.S. midterm results could accelerate India trade deal but raise tariff risks

Further, while it says that the 25% tariffs would be net of existing tariffs levied on India, meaning they will not add to the 10% already in effect, the order also said that it remained for the USTR to decide whether these new tariffs would be adjusted keeping in mind those other tariffs.
The Indian government said it has taken note of the actions by the USTR and that its notice is currently under examination.

“India engaged constructively throughout this investigation,” the statement by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry said. “In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.”

“India and the United States are engaged in negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement,” it added. “It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations. Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement, as announced on 2nd February 2026 and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026.”

The USTR had in March launched two separate investigations into American trade partners, including India, under Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act. The first investigation related to forced labour resulted in a tariff of 10% levied on India. The new tariffs announced on Wednesday are a result of the second investigation into structural excess capacity.

Apart from this, the U.S. also levies a tariff of 50% on imports of aluminium and steel from all countries under Section 232 of its Trade Expansion Act. The new tariffs will not be added to these. Under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, the U.S. government is also empowered to levy a tariff of up to 100% on countries, including India, that import large quantities of Russian oil. This tariff has been temporarily paused by U.S. President Donald Trump.

In its report on India, the USTR concluded that India’s acts, policies, and practices “create, sustain, or contribute to structural excess capacity” that burden or restrict U.S. commerce by harming U.S. producers and exporters through unfair competition and reduced commercial opportunities; harm the U.S. economy due to lost exports, trade deficits, and a diminished manufacturing sector; and create economic security risks for the U.S.

articles.title: Jensen Huang needs a new playbook for his second innings at Nvidia

fullParagraphs: Returning to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters in California on Monday (November 23, 2026), and standing on the ground floor of the atrium, Jensen Huang apologised to employees and vowed to be a better CEO

Within two weeks, Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder, went from being an AI rainmaker, whose chips and business ingenuity kick-started the AI revolution, to a sex-and-spy scandal-hit CEO, who quit the company he built from scratch and helmed for over three decades, and then returned as its boss once again after a band of tech billionaires intensely lobbied the Trump administration for his reinstatement.

Returning to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters in California on Monday (November 23, 2026), and standing on the ground floor of the atrium, Mr. Huang apologised to employees and vowed to be a better CEO as staff cheered to see their chief back, whose exit wiped out close to a quarter of the company’s market value. Mr. Huang’s return buoyed the market as Nvidia’s stock soared, adding nearly a trillion dollars in market value the day he was back at Nvidia.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: Jensen Huang needs a new playbook for his second innings at Nvidia. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: Plane crash off coast of Mississippi kills extended family of six on fishing trip
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Shortly before losing contact with the plane, an air traffic controller at Gulfport–Biloxi International Airport advised the pilot of precipitation and adverse weather in the area

Authorities are investigating why a small plane carrying six members of a Florida family crashed off the Mississippi coast on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). They were returning home from a fishing trip, relatives say.

The plane’s pilot was Brent Stokes, the 50-year-old president of a marine contracting company based in Fort Myers, according to Jackson County Coroner Bruce Lynd Jr. Stokes’ company’s website described him as an “avid fisherman and lifetime boater.”

This undated photo provided by Allyson Dickey on November 25, 2026, shows Brent Stokes, far right, alongside his wife Dominique Stokes, centre right, and their children, Addison, centre left, and Hunter. | Photo Credit: AP

The other victims were Stokes’ 16-year-old son, Hunter Stokes; Stokes’ sister, Arlyn Knox, 43; her husband, Michael Knox, 43; and their two sons, 12-year-old Charles Holden Knox and 10-year-old Truett Knox.
Arlyn and Michael Knox ran Knox Technologies, a Fort Myers-based IT company they founded in 2012, according to the company's website.
The Knox and Stokes families confirmed their deaths in an emailed statement provided to The Associated Press.

“They died doing what they loved: celebrating the start of a wonderful holiday season with a fishing trip together before heading home to be with the rest of our family,” the statement said. “In the middle of our grief, we are holding on to that and to how much love they gave us and how much love surrounds us now. We will carry them with us always.”
Lynd said that autopsies are being performed on Brent Stokes and Michael Knox, who was also a licensed pilot.

The air traffic control regional tower in Mobile, Alabama, reported at about 3:45 p.m. that it had lost contact with the aircraft, according to the Coast Guard. The closest National Weather Service station, in Pascagoula, shows there were light winds, no precipitation and clouds blanketing the sky in the area at the time of the crash.

The pilot doesn’t appear to have reported any problems when the plane took off from an airport in New Orleans or made a distress call during the flight, according to air traffic recordings publicly available on the website LiveATC.net .

articles.title: Bad weather postpones Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade for first time ever
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The postponement came as New York City is set to get slammed by a storm bringing intense winds and rain to the region
Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will also be a first: Organisers made an unprecedented decision to postpone the event to Saturday (November 28, 2026) because of bad weather.

The annual parade, originally scheduled for Thursday (November 26, 2026), has been moved “out of an abundance of caution” and following consultation with city officials about the severe weather, Macy’s said in a statement Wednesday.
“Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday, and we will share additional details as they are finalized,” the company said.

The postponement came as New York City is set to get slammed by a storm bringing intense winds and rain to the region, which had raised worries about how the parade’s massive balloons would fare while floating through the windswept canyons between Manhattan’s skyscrapers and over throngs of spectators lining the streets below.
At a news conference, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday’s winds will be strong enough to snap tree limbs and down power lines, and he stressed that rescheduling the parade was the right call.

“Now, I know that many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow,” he said. “Generation after generation has watched SpongeBob and Spider-Man soar down our streets and has taken in Garfield floating down Sixth Avenue. And I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first.”

The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning and a coastal flood warning for Thursday into Friday. The city’s emergency management agency has been warning residents about the possible storm, with officials banning empty tractor-trailers from bridges Thursday morning because of the wind.

NBC , which airs the parade, said it will instead broadcast a rerun of the 2025 edition on Thursday (November 26, 2026). It was not immediately clear whether the event’s expansive lineup would also shift to the new date, though representatives for Broadway shows “Chicago” and “Hamilton” said their performers will make the switch to Saturday (November 28, 2026).

The parade’s iconic balloons were well on the way to being inflated when the postponement was announced. Macy’s representatives had repeatedly put off interviews on-site, raising eyebrows among the city’s news media ahead of the official postponement.

Will Coss, a Macy’s executive, said organizers are working with bands and other performers and are “optimistic that we’re going to be able to maintain the parade that we set out to produce and to deliver to New York City on Thanksgiving.”

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

The postponement came as New York City is set to get slammed by a storm bringing intense winds and rain to the region

Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will also be a first: Organisers made an unprecedented decision to postpone the event to Saturday (November 28, 2026) because of bad weather.

The annual parade, originally scheduled for Thursday (November 26, 2026), has been moved “out of an abundance of caution” and following consultation with city officials about the severe weather, Macy’s said in a statement Wednesday.

“Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday, and we will share additional details as they are finalized,” the company said.

The postponement came as New York City is set to get slammed by a storm bringing intense winds and rain to the region, which had raised worries about how the parade’s massive balloons would fare while floating through the windswept canyons between Manhattan’s skyscrapers and over throngs of spectators lining the streets below.

At a news conference, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday’s winds will be strong enough to snap tree limbs and down power lines, and he stressed that rescheduling the parade was the right call.

“Now, I know that many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow,” he said. “Generation after generation has watched SpongeBob and Spider-Man soar down our streets and has taken in Garfield floating down Sixth Avenue. And I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first.”

The National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning and a coastal flood warning for Thursday into Friday. The city’s emergency management agency has been warning residents about the possible storm, with officials banning empty tractor-trailers from bridges Thursday morning because of the wind.

NBC , which airs the parade, said it will instead broadcast a rerun of the 2025 edition on Thursday (November 26, 2026). It was not immediately clear whether the event’s expansive lineup would also shift to the new date, though representatives for Broadway shows “Chicago” and “Hamilton” said their performers will make the switch to Saturday (November 28, 2026).

The parade’s iconic balloons were well on the way to being inflated when the postponement was announced. Macy’s representatives had repeatedly put off interviews on-site, raising eyebrows among the city’s news media ahead of the official postponement.

Will Coss, a Macy’s executive, said organizers are working with bands and other performers and are “optimistic that we’re going to be able to maintain the parade that we set out to produce and to deliver to New York City on Thanksgiving.”

articles.title: Jensen Huang won’t need a pardon, says U.S. Vice President, as scrutiny of Nvidia scandal builds in Washington
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: U.S. Vice President JD Vance is downplaying the possibility that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could need a pardon from President Donald Trump

U.S. Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday played down the possibility that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could need a presidential pardon just days before the executive of the AI giant is expected to appear before a congressional committee.

Mr. Vance told reporters that Justice Department officials and “multiple officials in our national security apparatus” have confirmed that Mr. Huang is “under no investigation.” The vice president made the remarks after having a Thanksgiving Eve meal with troops at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.

The Nvidia CEO resigned earlier this month after acknowledging extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. He was reinstated 11 days later at the urging of U.S. President Donald Trump.

“I don’t think he needs a pardon at all,” Mr. Vance said. “I haven’t seen any evidence again that he committed a crime. And if there is evidence that he committed a crime, then that’s up to relevant authorities to actually bring a prosecution against him.”

Mr. Trump also told the Post he doesn't want Mr. Huang to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights under the U.S. Constitution to avoid self-incrimination amid potential criminal prosecution when he appears before lawmakers. Pleading the Fifth allows a person to refuse to answer questions or provide testimonial evidence if doing so could reasonably expose them to criminal prosecution.

Mr. Huang is scheduled to appear for a closed-door transcribed interview with a trio of panels on December 1, including the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs committees, and the Select Committee on China. Then on December 3, Mr. Huang is expected to appear at a public hearing of the Senate Banking Committee.
The board’s stunning reversal has spurred questions about its independence and what Mr. Trump’s role means for the meeting of business and politics.
Nvidia and the White House are also facing scrutiny about Mr. Trump's relationship with Mr. Huang, a close adviser to the president on artificial intelligence issues.

The president has repeatedly welcomed Mr. Huang to the White House and earlier this year invited him aboard Air Force One for a state visit to China. The New York Times has reported that Mr. Trump had previously been briefed on intelligence concerns about the Nvidia CEO's relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed. U.S. officials suspected that she was working with China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has denied it.

Congressional staffers from the House and Senate Intelligence Committees and representing chamber leaders received a classified briefing on Tuesday about the matter from intelligence officials, according to two people familiar with the matter who were not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity.

articles.title: India’s satellite supply chain ‘highly dependent on imports’, says space body
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to grow to $40-45 billion in less than a decade

India’s satellite supply chain is “highly dependent” on imports for critical components and the private sector’s contribution is limited to “structural assemblies” and “propulsion components” largely supplied by established public sector firms and vintage private firms, said a report by IN-SPACe, India’s regulatory-cum-promotional body for the private space sector.
While pointing out the potential of India’s private space companies, the autonomous body under the Department of Space underlined the challenges ahead.

Science Minister Jitendra Singh earlier this week said that India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to increase to $40-45 billion in less than a decade, with the private sector set to grow from a a few startups “to nearly 400-500 companies in just a few years”.

The Supply Chain Landscape of Satellite Manufacturing in India report, which was made public on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), says that nearly 60% of satellite costs were attributed to electronic, electrical and electromechanical components, and specialised materials, many of which are imported.
India also has limited testing and certification facilities, which weakened prospects for acceptance in global markets.
Many companies largely operated on a “project-based manufacturing model”, which disincentivised long-term investment in automation and production capacity, the report noted.
Critical components often took a long time to procure – frequently 12-16 months – which led to project delays and hobbled responsiveness to market opportunities.

There was also a shortage of trained and skilled personnel in satellite systems engineering, quality assurance, testing and qualification, besides limited private-sector research and development and technology transfer.
The report was prepared by Brijesh Kumar Sol and Yudhishthir J. of IN-SPACe and “approved” by Pawan Goenka, IN-SPACe chairman.
The report isn’t a statistical survey, but paints a descriptive map of India’s satellite manufacturing supply chain.

articles.title: Experts say new U.S. tariffs do not pose substantial threat, India should not rush into trade deal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The latest proposal by the USTR takes the tariff framework on India back to what it was at the start of trade deal negotiations

The new 25% tariffs proposed by the U.S. on India do not pose a substantial risk to Indian exports, and India should go ahead with a trade deal only if it is balanced and reciprocal, according to exporters and trade and tariff experts.

An analysis of India’s trade relationship with the U.S. over the last two years showed that the latest tariffs announced by the U.S. have returned the tariff relationship to where it was at the start of trade deal negotiations.
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed a net tariff of 25% on goods imported from India, which could be reduced to 17% if a trade deal is signed by the two countries.

The proposed 25% tariff is nearly the same as the 26% tariff U.S. President Donald Trump had originally proposed in his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariff measure in April 2025. A week later, Mr. Trump paused these tariffs in a bid to secure trade deals with other countries.

In July 2025, he announced a 25% tariff on India, the same as what the USTR is now proposing. But Mr. Trump soon announced an additional 25% tariff as a penalty for India’s Russian oil imports taking the total tariff on Indian goods to 50%.

During that time, Mr. Trump also announced a 50% tariff on the import of steel and aluminium from all countries. The latest tariffs by the USTR are not in addition to those tariffs, meaning Indian steel and aluminium will continue to attract a 50% duty.

In February 2026, India and the U.S. issued a joint statement announcing the framework for an interim deal on trade, under which the U.S. would reduce its tariffs on Indian goods to 18%. This is very close to the 17% the U.S. is proposing now, should a deal be signed, nearly 10 months after the joint statement was issued.
As such, the pre-deal, post-deal, and steel and aluminium tariffs by the U.S. on India largely remain where they were at the start of negotiations.
Exporters and trade experts have said that India should proceed with a trade deal only if it satisfies Indian interests.

“FIEO supports the government’s efforts to conclude the Bilateral Trade Agreement at an early date,” said S.C. Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations. “The agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India’s long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level-playing field with suppliers from other countries in the U.S. market.”

articles.title: Vellappally Natesan says he has ‘no differences’ with Keralam CM Satheesan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The remarks came against the backdrop of repeated criticism and exchanges between Natesan and Satheesan before UDF came to power following Assembly election earlier this year

Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan on Thursday said he had “no differences” with Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, signalling a softening of his stand towards the Congress leader after a series of public exchanges between them.
The SNDP Yogam represents the numerically strong Ezhava community in Keralam.

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Natesan said there had been no differences between him and Mr. Satheesan. “There are no differences with me in the first place. So, why should we talk about reconciliation,” he asked.
The remarks came against the backdrop of repeated criticism and exchanges between Mr. Natesan and Mr. Satheesan before the UDF came to power following the Assembly election earlier this year.
Asked about his past criticism of Mr. Satheesan, Mr. Natesan said there was no difference in his assessment of the Congress leader “then and now.”
“I have only expressed my views on specific issues,” he said.
Mr. Natesan said he had criticised Mr. Satheesan for “an immature stand” and for not respecting the Opposition when the latter was the Leader of the Opposition during the previous government.
When asked whether Mr. Satheesan has matured since becoming the Chief Minister, he said: “It is only six months. Let’s wait and see.”

Mr. Natesan said it was Nair Service Society (NSS) general secretary G. Sukumaran Nair who had earlier announced that Mr. Satheesan would not be allowed into the organisation’s office, adding that he had never objected to the Chief Minister visiting the SNDP premises.
“I have never objected to anyone coming here. It was the NSS leadership that announced such a restriction,” he said.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the Centre, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke , Saurav Das , Ashutosh Ranka and others.
Senior advocate Mahesh Jethmalani appeared for the lawyers’ body.

The petition argued that while dissent is part of democracy, protests must stay within legal bounds and avoid paralysing the capital or disrupting lawyers’ livelihoods.

“Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondents to review, modify, formulate and implement a standard operating procedure [SOP] for dealing with public protests conducted in violation of applicable law, lawful restrictions or valid directions of the competent authorities, ensuring timely, coordinated action to ensure normal public life,” the plea said.
The petition referred to the protests organised by CJP during July and October, 2026.

Permission was sought and granted for a single day on June 20, 2026 again, confined to the hours between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m., but the demonstration was not discontinued at the expiry of the permitted hours, it said.

“No extension was ever granted, and that the organisers unilaterally announced an indefinite sit-in in the absence of any permission. fullParagraphs: PM Modi said the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, one that will continue to guide in realising the resolve of a developed India

Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan called for respecting all languages and cautioned against looking down upon other people’s mother tongues, saying that respect for one’s own language must go hand in hand with respect for the languages of others.

“If I don’t respect the sentiments of others, then I don’t deserve that my sentiments will be respected by others,” Mr. Radhakrishnan said, stressing that linguistic diversity should be a source of mutual respect and national unity.

Addressing an event organised by the Union Law Ministry to mark the 77th anniversary of the adoption of the Constitution, he released its updated versions in all 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule.

Describing the initiative as a celebration of India’s linguistic diversity and democratic inclusiveness, the Vice-President said making the Constitution available in different languages would bring governance closer to the people and enable citizens to understand the country’s foundational document in their mother tongues.

“Our Constitution is our pride and our duty,” he said, adding that the availability of the document in multiple languages reflected the spirit of Jan Bhagidari and the collective responsibility of citizens in upholding constitutional values.
He also cautioned against equating knowledge with proficiency in English, saying it was just another language like any Indian mother tongue.
“Never think that speaking in English is knowledge. English is also one of the languages like our mother tongue. It’s nothing more,” he said.
“If our nation is not protected, none of our languages will be protected,” he said, urging citizens to work with the spirit of ‘Rashtra Pratham’ (Nation First). — PTI

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Opposition parties on Thursday (November 26, 2026) of weakening the Constitution and democratic institutions, saying those who had attempted to “strangle the Constitution” when in power were now carrying a red book to mislead people.
He criticised Congress for “disrespecting Ambedkar”, and alleged that the party did not confer the Bharat Ratna on him and conspired to prevent him from entering Parliament.

articles.title: 10 years and doubled cost: The four-laning saga of Mangaluru-Bengaluru NH 75 in Dakshina Kannada and Hassan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The key highway connecting the state capital with coastal Karnataka becomes completely four-lane except the 26 km stretch of Shiradi Ghat between Maranahalli and Addahole

In the decadal saga of widening about 115 km stretch of Bengaluru-Mangaluru National Highway 75 between Hassan and B.C. Road in Dakshina Kannada district (excluding the 26-km Shiradi Ghat stretch), the total project cost has close to doubled, from about ₹1,220 crore estimated in the year 2017 to about ₹2,220 crore when the project was almost complete by 2026-end.

While the travel time (by a car) has reduced to about three-four hours between Hassan and Mangaluru from about five hours, road users endured tremendous ordeal during the past decade when the construction was underway, with the project witnessing an almost complete halt between 2018 and 2021 . Driving from Mangaluru to Hassan had become a nightmarish experience during this period.

While the Union Road Transport Ministry handed over the highway stretch to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in July 2016 to widen the stretch into a four-lane road, contracts were awarded to M/s Isolux Corson for the Hassan-Maranahalli stretch (about 50 km) at an estimated cost of ₹400 crore and M/s Larsen and Tubro for the Addahole-B C Road stretch (about 65 km) for ₹821 crore in 2017.

Within about 20 months, M/s Isolux declared insolvency and left the Hassan project while M/s Larsen submitted a letter of foreclosure as the NHAI wanted to change the scope of the project and refused to revise the project cost by about ₹140 crore for the changed scope. The Authority spent a good about two years in choosing new contractors for the Dakshina Kannada stretch and arranging the sub-contractor M/s Rajkamal Builders, to continue the Hassan district work.

The abnormally slow pace of construction, notwithstanding Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari’s claim of constructing about 40 km highway in a day, irritated road users as well as general public in the vicinity of the project highway.

With the contractors seldom following proper construction methods, including providing motorable alternative roads during the construction period, road users struggled to negotiate pothole and crater-ridden highway for years. While clouds of dust engulfed the highway during summer, the stretch was riddled with slush during the rainy season for years. Kalladka Town near B.C. Road where the NHAI built a 3 km elevated road (flyover) due to public demand, suffered massively for almost five years during the construction period.

While the project highway is almost complete except for about 1 km at two places in Dakshina Kannada district, the NHAI needs to take measures to ensure pedestrian safety at many places, including Mani, Uppinangady, Melkar, and other places as the vehicles move at high speed on the newly built wide carriageways.

Road users are also upset at the speed being limited to 80 kmph on the widened section with one user quipping, “Earlier, it was impossible to drive; now we cannot drive.” However, NHAI has justified the restrictions saying the carriageways are designed for those particular limits.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 26 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 10 years and doubled cost: The four-laning saga of Mangaluru-Bengaluru NH 75 in Dakshina Kannada and Hassan

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

The key highway connecting the state capital with coastal Karnataka becomes completely four-lane except the 26 km stretch of Shiradi Ghat between Maranahalli and Addahole

In the decadal saga of widening about 115 km stretch of Bengaluru-Mangaluru National Highway 75 between Hassan and B.C. Road in Dakshina Kannada district (excluding the 26-km Shiradi Ghat stretch), the total project cost has close to doubled, from about ₹1,220 crore estimated in the year 2017 to about ₹2,220 crore when the project was almost complete by 2026-end.

While the travel time (by a car) has reduced to about three-four hours between Hassan and Mangaluru from about five hours, road users endured tremendous ordeal during the past decade when the construction was underway, with the project witnessing an almost complete halt between 2018 and 2021 . Driving from Mangaluru to Hassan had become a nightmarish experience during this period.

While the Union Road Transport Ministry handed over the highway stretch to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in July 2016 to widen the stretch into a four-lane road, contracts were awarded to M/s Isolux Corson for the Hassan-Maranahalli stretch (about 50 km) at an estimated cost of ₹400 crore and M/s Larsen and Tubro for the Addahole-B C Road stretch (about 65 km) for ₹821 crore in 2017.

Within about 20 months, M/s Isolux declared insolvency and left the Hassan project while M/s Larsen submitted a letter of foreclosure as the NHAI wanted to change the scope of the project and refused to revise the project cost by about ₹140 crore for the changed scope. The Authority spent a good about two years in choosing new contractors for the Dakshina Kannada stretch and arranging the sub-contractor M/s Rajkamal Builders, to continue the Hassan district work.

The abnormally slow pace of construction, notwithstanding Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari’s claim of constructing about 40 km highway in a day, irritated road users as well as general public in the vicinity of the project highway.

With the contractors seldom following proper construction methods, including providing motorable alternative roads during the construction period, road users struggled to negotiate pothole and crater-ridden highway for years. While clouds of dust engulfed the highway during summer, the stretch was riddled with slush during the rainy season for years. Kalladka Town near B.C. Road where the NHAI built a 3 km elevated road (flyover) due to public demand, suffered massively for almost five years during the construction period.

While the project highway is almost complete except for about 1 km at two places in Dakshina Kannada district, the NHAI needs to take measures to ensure pedestrian safety at many places, including Mani, Uppinangady, Melkar, and other places as the vehicles move at high speed on the newly built wide carriageways.

Road users are also upset at the speed being limited to 80 kmph on the widened section with one user quipping, “Earlier, it was impossible to drive; now we cannot drive.” However, NHAI has justified the restrictions saying the carriageways are designed for those particular limits.

3.
